contributes.instructions: Pasting HTML on the canvas (Cmd+V with markup as plain text, or text/html that is more than a single paragraph of prose; a paragraph copied from a page lands as canvas text through the Text plugin instead) lands it as one new daydream.viewport page, 960px wide and selected. The page is what was pasted: every <style> block's text, in document order, is its css, verbatim, and the rest of the markup is its html — the pasted text as it arrived when there was nothing to gather out of it, the browser's serialization when there was. The document's <title> is the page's meta title. A linked stylesheet is not fetched: it is removed and reported. A data: image is stored through the host and its img points at assets/<file>; one that cannot be stored loses its src, and the img stays with its alt. The paste does not run the landing's cleaning yet: what could run stays in the stored html and the canvas removes it at every mount. No gates run on a paste; the console reports what was lost. A paste of more than 10,000 elements or four million characters is refused and lands nothing.
